question: What is the difference between two coterminal angles?
solution:
Rotating more or less by a whole number of full revolutions returns the terminal side to the same position. Conversely, with the same initial side, returning to the same terminal side requires a whole number of full revolutions. Thus the difference between coterminal angles is \(k\cdot360^\circ\), where \(k\) is any integer, including zero. D gives this exact characterization.

However, \(k\cdot360^\circ=(2k)\cdot180^\circ\), so A also holds for every coterminal pair. A is weaker: \(0^\circ\) and \(180^\circ\) differ by an integer multiple of \(180^\circ\) but have different terminal sides. Therefore A and D are both true as written; D is uniquely intended only if the question asks for an exact characterization.
